title: events.json — coded events contract
description: All newly coded events for a publication cycle (system prompt §3.3, §5). Schema-enforced rules: corroboration for Tier ≥ 3 (two S3+ sources incl. one S1/S2; the ≥5-point-delta half of the rule is checked in the pipeline where deltas exist), no S5-only sourcing, analyst inference explicitly tagged, corrections referencing the corrected event. Doc 07 F-2/F-7: direction is no longer coded here — controller_id is required and direction is derived at the edge level from the controller; reversals are marked is_reversal:true and carry reversal_of, resolved by validate.py check_reversal_target (not schema, since resolution is cross-file). Not schema-enforceable (pipeline/review-UI responsibility): source *independence*, the two-S4-cannot-corroborate rule, the Goodhart 2-point cap, Tier-1/2 decay, controller_id/counterparty_id/actor_id/reversal_of resolution, direction/pole derivation correctness.

date.description: True event date, not capture date.

controller_id.description: Doc 07 F-2: required, resolves into controllers.json (validate.py check_controller_resolution). Direction is no longer coded here — it is derived at the edge level from the controller.

counterparty_ids.description: Doc 07 F-7 rule 7: controller ≠ counterparty. A committed tenant on a locally-operated facility holds a real panopticon position and belongs as its own event (operator at Facilities, tenant at Cloud/Models, one bundle_id) — counterparty_ids records the relationship without collapsing it.

actor_id.description: Doc 07 F-7 rule 8: on a reversal event, controller_id names the controller of the thing reversed; actor_id names the entity that did the reversing, when distinct.

is_reversal.description: Doc 01 §2.1: reversals score ×(−1) of the tier reversed. Direction is no longer coded, so this — not direction=reversal — is what marks an event as a reversal; reversal_of is then required (validate.py check_reversal_target, doc 07 F-7 rule 8).

reversal_of.description: Doc 07 F-7 rule 8: reversals are never uncodeable — a reference to a coded event or edge, or (for facts predating coded collection) an inline reversal_target. Resolution is checked by validate.py check_reversal_target, not schema.

p_subindicators_evidenced.description: Which P sub-indicators this event evidences, when depth_dimensions includes P.

summary.description: Analyst's own-words summary (§2.3 no verbatim reproduction).

analyst_inference.description: §2.3: analyst judgment is tagged and rendered separately from observed events.

correction.description: Corrections append; prior events are immutable (§2.3).

bundle_anchor.description: §3.4: the layer carrying the financing, set on exactly one event per bundle (pipeline-checked).

sub_state_actor.description: Doc 01 §5: the sub-state entity the commitment actually attaches to.

contested_decision.description: Doc 01 §5: intra-government contestation over a procurement — high-information signal.

verified_value_usd.description: Recorded separately from announced; announced values are routinely inflated (§2.2).

allOf.$comment: Corroboration rule, §2.2: Tier ≥ 3 requires two S3-or-better sources, at least one of them S1/S2.
S5 is never scored (§2.2): every published event must have at least one S1–S4 source.
Tagged inference must carry its rationale.
A correction must reference the event it corrects.
